outcome: pelvic diaphragm hiatus parameters (UVJ-M, A(r), A(v), th, D(r), D(v), ARJ-VDv, CV-VD, ARJ-VD)
cohort: The study included 40 women who had a vaginal delivery and 40 women who had a selective cesarean section between November 2018 and December 2020.
finding: Pelvic floor function 6-8 weeks postpartum was significantly more affected in women who underwent vaginal delivery compared to those who had a selective cesarean section.
mod_finding: Selective cesarean section was found to have a certain but limited protective effect on maternal pelvic floor tissue compared to vaginal delivery.
